plans.objective: [DIM: optimization] The apparent flatness of N_c(w) for rigid families is an optimization artifact: small networks get stuck in local minima, falsely indicating rigidity when they simply fail to converge to the true solution.

steps.description: Implement the `family` function to define rigid (linear) and fat (quadratic) constraint families for the capacity scan experiment. This addresses the core scientific question of whether network capacity trends reflect solution space rigidity. The code must construct training/holdout points as (N,1) arrays, ensure non-overlapping holdout sets, and return the required dictionary format. The capacity_scan pipeline (already built in the sandbox) will handle the L-BFGS-B optimization, multi-start sampling, and N_c(w) computation.

plans.objective: [DIM: optimization] The apparent flatness of N_c(w) for rigid families is an optimization artifact: small networks get stuck in local minima, failing to reach the zero-violation regime even when theoretically possible.

steps.description: [auto-routed: surprise=1.00] Implement the rigid and fat constraint families as required by the capacity_scan interface, ensuring the rigid family is a low-dimensional linear system (e.g., linear constraints with unique solution) and the fat family is a high-dimensional continuous family (e.g., linear constraints with null space). This will enable testing the hypothesis that small networks fail to reach zero violation for rigid families due to optimization artifacts. The family function must return properly shaped training/validation data without overlap, using scipy.optimize.minimize with L-BFGS-B for optimization (as per protocol). The code should be saved to /workspace/research_outputs/shusheng_rsi_run26/family.py so the existing run() can import it.
